story: Pere Marquette State Park sits where the Illinois River meets the Mississippi. Hundreds of bald eagles gather here in late winter to catch fish, a comeback that began in the 1990s. In the rivers, mussel beds have dwindled and invasive Asian carp have partly replaced native fish.
matters: About 230 bird species have been logged here, across 8,050 acres of bluffs, wetlands and forest at the meeting of two great rivers.
